newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A new prime minister and cabinet will be selected on Saturday. New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is the likely person to become the new prime minister in the absence of any strong challenger, a government source said. But the final decision must be made with agreement by the six coalition parties. (BANGKOK POST)
- Nearly 40 percent of the country's district hospitals suffer from a shortage of doctors, with some having no doctor at all, a recent Rural Doctors Society survey says. (THE NATION)

- Queen Elizabeth II of Britain will witness a spectacular Royal Barge procession rehearsal along the Chao Phya River when she visits Thailand as guest of the king and queen late next month, a senior navy officer says. (THE NATION)

- The state-run Government Savings Bank is prepared to sign agreements with brokerage firms on October 5 on its 10 billion baht support fund. The fund is designed to help stock market investors whose might be forced to sell their shares by brokers. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- Thai Airways International plans to take 80 percent of the profits from the country's first national cargo airline although it will have only a 40 percent stake in the venture. The shareholding guidelines for the establishment of the cargo service airline are scheduled to go before the THAI board for approval today. (BANGKOK POST)

- Unocal Thailand Co will spend US$1.39 billion over the next five years developing its natural gas field in the Gulf of Thailand. Under the five-year plan, the company will focus on the gas fields needed to fulfill four natural gas contracts with the Petroleum Authority of Thailand. (THE NATION)
- The Bank of Thailand says it is serious about curbing short-term foreign borrowing but it is not going to hastily impose measures to control short-term foreign borrowing. (BUSINESS DAY)
